content: Whatever sits before la becomes the
CONTEXT for the sentence after it —
Toki Pona's all-purpose if/when/
as-for:
ken la = maybe, possibly
(possibility, given that...)
mi la, ni li pona.
= In my opinion, this is good.
sina wile e pona la, sina o pali.
= If you want good things, work.
(condition before la, result after)
tenpo ni la = right now, these days
(a time context before la)

trigger_word: sina moku ala moku e moku ni?
title: LESSON 9: E — MARKING THE OBJECT

content: e marks the DIRECT OBJECT — the
thing a verb happens TO:
mi wile e telo.  = I want water.
mi lukin e ni.   = I'm looking at
this.
NEGATING: ala slots in right before
the e, straight after the verb:
sina moku ala moku e moku ni?
= Are you eating this food or not?
mi wile ala e telo nasa.
= I don't want alcohol.
(wile ala e X = don't want X)
